<SPAN 1>This Non-Circumvention, Non-Disclosure </SPAN 1><SPAN 2>Agreement (the “Agreement”) is entered into by and between We Rock The Spectrum Kid’s Gym, LLC (“WRTS”), 5520 Crebs Avenue, Tarzana, California 91356, USA (“Disclosing Party”) and _______________, located at _______________ (“Receiving Party”) for the purpose of preventing the unauthorized disclosure of Conﬁdential Information as deﬁned below. </SPAN 2><SPAN 3>The parties agree to enter into a conﬁdential relationship with respect to the disclosure of certain proprietary and conﬁdential information (“Conﬁdential Information”). </SPAN 3><SPAN 4>The undersigned Parties agree in consideration of their mutual promises to abide by the following terms and conditions:</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>1. Definition of Confidential Information. </SPAN 5><SPAN 6>For purposes of this Agreement, “Confidential Information” shall include all information or material that has or could have commercial value or other utility in the business in which Disclosing Party is engaged. </SPAN 6><SPAN 7>Such information shall include, but not be limited to contracts, documents, files, printouts, websites, and other printed and digital information provided by the Disclosing party and also the names, telephone numbers, addresses, fax numbers, email addresses, etc. of the contact, parties, and/or source(s) provided by the Disclosing Party. </SPAN 7><SPAN 8>The Parties acknowledge that the Confidential Information may be written, oral, graphic, pictorial, recorded, or stored and transmitted in digital form or any digital format; and such information is deemed valuable, special or unique assets of the Disclosing Party that were developed or obtained through investment of significant time, efforts and expense, and that access to such information would not be possible but for the relationship of the Parties hereunder.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>2. Exclusions from Confidential Information. </SPAN 9><SPAN 10>Receiving Party's obligations under this Agreement do not extend to information that is: </SPAN 10><SPAN 11>(a) publicly known at the time of disclosure or subsequently becomes publicly known through no fault of the Receiving Party; </SPAN 11><SPAN 12>(b) discovered or created by the Receiving Party before disclosure by Disclosing Party; </SPAN 12><SPAN 13>(c) learned by the Receiving Party through legitimate means other than from the Disclosing Party or Disclosing Party's representatives; or </SPAN 13><SPAN 14>(d) is disclosed by Receiving Party with Disclosing Party's prior written approval.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>3. Pre-Existing Relationships. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>In the event that any third parties already have a pre-existing working relationship or have previously made contact with any parties to this Agreement via other means, and such third parties were not introduced by any parties to this Agreement, such third party contacts and/ or sources are not subject to the restrictions, terms and conditions of this Agreement.</SPAN 16>
<SPAN 17>4. Obligations of Receiving Party. </SPAN 17><SPAN 18>Receiving Party shall hold and maintain the Confidential Information in strictest confidence for the sole and exclusive benefit of the Disclosing Party. </SPAN 18><SPAN 19>Receiving Party shall carefully restrict access to Confidential Information to any employees, contractors, agents, and any other third parties as is reasonably required and shall require those persons to sign non-disclosure restrictions at least as protective as those in this Agreement. </SPAN 19><SPAN 20>Receiving Party shall not, without prior written approval of Disclosing Party, use for Receiving Party's own benefit, publish, copy, transmit, use, or otherwise disclose to others, or permit the use by others for their benefit or to the detriment of Disclosing Party, any Confidential Information. </SPAN 20><SPAN 21>Receiving Party shall return to Disclosing Party any and all records, documents, graphics, electronic files, notes, and other written, printed, or electronic copies, or other tangible materials or digital files in its possession pertaining to Confidential Information immediately if Disclosing Party requests it in writing.</SPAN 21>
<SPAN 22>5. Time Periods. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>The nondisclosure provisions of this Agreement shall survive the termination of this Agreement and Receiving Party's duty to hold Confidential Information in confidence shall remain in effect until the Confidential Information no longer qualifies as a trade secret or until Disclosing Party sends Receiving Party written notice releasing Receiving Party from this Agreement, whichever occurs first.</SPAN 23>
<SPAN 24>6. Non-Circumvention. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>The Receiving Party expressly agrees not to circumvent, avoid, bypass or obviate the Disclosing Party in any manner, directly or indirectly, to avoid payment of fees, royalties, or any other obligation in any way involving any of the parties introduced and Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to this Agreement, or any transaction contemplated hereunder or other business arrangement arising out of or connected in any way to the Confidential Information.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>7. Return of Confidential Information. </SPAN 26><SPAN 27>Unless a business agreement, contract, or other business arrangement is entered into, each Party agrees to return or destroy, with written confirmation, all Confidential Information in any form upon conclusion of the evaluation of entering into the transaction or other business arrangement or upon the specific request of the Disclosing Party.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>8. Independent Contractors. </SPAN 28><SPAN 29>Each party is an independent contractor with respect to the other, and nothing in this Agreement will be deemed to place the parties in the relationship of employer-employee, principal-agent, franchisee-franchisor, partners, or joint ventures. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Neither party shall have authority to bind the other except to the extent authorized herein.</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>9. Integration. </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>The Parties agree that this Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement and the understanding of the Parties concerning subject matter hereof and this Agreement supersedes all previous communications, proposals, representations and agreements, whether oral or written, relating thereto, among these parties. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>This Agreement may not be amended except in a writing signed by both Parties.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>10. Severability. </SPAN 34><SPAN 35>Should any provisions at this Agreement be held by a court of law to be illegal, invalid or unenforceable, the legality, validity and enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall not be affected or impaired thereby and shall continue to be in effect.</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>11. Waiver. </SPAN 36><SPAN 37>The failure to exercise any right provided in this Agreement shall not be a waiver of prior or subsequent rights.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>12. Governing Law. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>All matters affecting the interpretation of this Agreement and the rights of the parties hereto shall be governed by the laws of the United States and the State of California, without reference to rules governing choice of laws.</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>This Agreement and each party's obligations shall be binding on the representatives, assigns, and successors of such party. </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>Each party has signed this Agreement through its authorized representative. </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>We Rock the Spectrum Kid’s Gym, </SPAN 42><SPAN 43>_________________________________</SPAN 43>
<SPAN 44>Disclosing Party Receiving Party</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>By: </SPAN 45><SPAN 46>______________________________ </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>By: </SPAN 47><SPAN 48>_____________________________</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>Dina L. Kimmel - President/CEO</SPAN 49>

guidance.when: Assessing whether return or destruction is required upon termination of the agreement.
guidance.inspection: Identify both the required act and its triggering event. A duty triggered only by the discloser's request does not establish a termination-triggered duty; termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, or abandonment must itself activate the duty.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative return-or-destruction duty together with language linking it to termination or an equivalent end event.

guidance.when: The agreement contains an exception to a return or destruction obligation.
guidance.inspection: Check whether the exception expressly permits continued possession of backups, archival material, a legal copy, or another defined subset after the return/destruction event. Conditions on access, purpose, or continuing confidentiality do not negate the permission.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the retention exception and, when separated, the governing return/destruction clause showing the temporal context.

guidance.when: The agreement requires return or destruction of confidential information and copies without stating a retention exception.
guidance.inspection: Determine whether the duty is exhaustive as to the covered material and copies. A complete return/destruction command that leaves no authorized retained subset negates permission to possess some material afterward.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the exhaustive operative duty and verify across the complete agreement that no backup, archival, legal-copy, or other retention exception qualifies it.

guidance.when: The agreement addresses ownership, licenses, or rights in confidential information or associated intellectual property.
guidance.inspection: Look for language that no license or right is granted, conveyed, conferred, or implied. A limited authorization to review or use information for the stated transaction does not by itself contradict the broader no-grant proposition.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the express no-grant clause; include an ownership clause only when it helps establish the object of the denied rights.

guidance.when: The agreement restricts disclosure of negotiations, discussions, a contemplated transaction, or the existence of dealings between the parties.
guidance.inspection: Treat a prohibition on revealing that negotiations or discussions are occurring as covering the fact of the agreement or negotiation, even when the restriction is framed as disclosure to the public or media rather than as secrecy of the document itself.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the prohibition and the text identifying the protected fact; retain any governing introduction needed to show that the listed fact is prohibited from disclosure.

guidance.when: Confidential-information coverage is conditioned on marking, designation, or identification by the disclosing party.
guidance.inspection: Confirm that every covered disclosure mode is subject to an express identification mechanism, including any oral or non-written mode. A universal marking rule may use different procedures for written and oral disclosures.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite all clauses needed to cover each disclosure mode and its identification requirement; do not rely on one mode while another remains unconditional.

guidance.when: The definition covers information either expressly designated confidential or reasonably understood to be confidential from its nature or disclosure circumstances.
guidance.inspection: The contextual alternative independently covers undesignated information, so express identification by the disclosing party is not required for all confidential information.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the complete alternative definition showing both designation and circumstance- or nature-based coverage.

guidance.when: Assessing whether the receiving party may make any copy in some circumstance.
guidance.inspection: Find an express copying route, such as prior written consent, copies needed for authorized persons, or automatic backup creation acknowledged by the agreement. Permission may be conditional and need not be general.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite language expressly addressing copying, reproduction, or backup creation and the condition that authorizes it; access or disclosure permission alone is insufficient.

guidance.when: The agreement expressly prohibits copying confidential information.
guidance.inspection: If copying is barred and the complete agreement provides no condition under which the receiving party may copy, the conditional-copy permission hypothesis is negated. A consent exception would instead be a permission circumstance.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the copy prohibition and verify that no consent, operational-copy, backup, or other copying exception appears elsewhere.

guidance.when: The agreement permits disclosure to representatives or other persons.
guidance.inspection: Resolve who falls within the permitted class. Consultants, agents, counsel, accountants, professional advisers, affiliates, and similar non-employees establish sharing with some third parties; an employee-only exception does not.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite both the permission and the definition or enumeration proving that at least one permitted recipient is a third party, plus any need-to-know or confidentiality condition governing the permission.

guidance.when: The agreement states an authorized transaction, project, evaluation, business relationship, or other defined purpose for confidential information.
guidance.inspection: A command to use confidential information only for that purpose, or not for any other purpose, directly imposes the limited-use obligation. The existence of the authorized purpose is not a contradiction.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Cite the operative use restriction and enough purpose language to identify the authorized scope.

guidance.when: Relevant candidate text is a numbered item, exception, continuation, anaphoric clause, or otherwise incomplete fragment.
guidance.inspection: Read the governing introduction and adjacent items to determine the item's legal function, trigger, subject, and exceptions. Keep independent operative clauses separately; do not treat a neighboring item as evidence merely because it shares the list.
guidance.evidence_requirement: Include every span necessary to make the relied-on proposition complete, while excluding sibling items that do not establish that proposition.
